text:
My dear Mother and Father,

I cannot say that camp is all I could wish, though I would not call it unsatisfactory; the food is disagreeable, and my companion in the cabin sleeps with a noise I never met with before. Yesterday we went out upon the lake in a boat, and I overturned it, and all were amused at my expense; my mortification was extreme.

But there is a girl of the name of Kayla, who is really very agreeable; she is from Ohio, and knows a great deal about horses. We walk by the lake after dinner, and talk of nothing in particular; I flatter myself that she likes me, but I am not certain of it.

Be so good as to send more refreshments, and the little device without which my instrument is useless, and which I entirely forgot; the advisers are somewhat strict, but for the most part satisfactory.

Your affectionate son, Jake.

P.S. I beg that you will not suffer Max to use my apartment.
